summary.text: Tacit offers private TAC payments, Bitcoin asset issuance, DeFi pools and web apps.
Its homepage now leads with the live TAC payment chain, which settles on Ethereum.
Users sign in with a wallet or passkey, then shield assets, pay, swap, farm or borrow.
TAC moves between Bitcoin and Ethereum through proofs, the project says.
Private payment balances hold shares whose value rises with retained fees, according to Tacit.
Sending retains 0.002 TAC for that pool plus a variable gas fee, its documentation states.
The separate Pay and DeFi pools exchange assets through public withdrawals and fresh deposits, the project says.
Borrowing controls sit with a wallet configured for two approvals among five owners, according to Ethereum reads.
The legal operator is not identified in the sources read, and Tacit’s paper still lists four wallet owners.

lines.text: Tacit describes itself as private DeFi across Bitcoin and Ethereum.
Tacit says users can shield, swap, send, earn and borrow from one tacit1 ID.
lines.quote: shield, swap, send, earn and borrow

lines.text: Tacit says its DeFi pool can swap, farm, borrow, send and bridge to Bitcoin.
Tacit says its Pay pool can shield, pay privately, withdraw and create deposit addresses.
Tacit says its chain lets people hold TAC privately and pay anyone.
Bankless described Tacit as combining confidential tokens, a mixer, a private AMM and wrapped BTC on 1 June 2026.
Tacit says its Ethereum confidential pool accepts private transactions only with an SP1 zero-knowledge proof.
Tacit says its DeFi and Pay pools share nothing on chain; moving between them combines a public withdrawal and a shield.
Tacit says each payment is proved on the payer device and each block is checked on Ethereum.
Tacit says Bitcoin and Ethereum state cross by proof-of-work and an Ethereum light client.
Bankless says Tacit uses an indexer validation system that derives results from on-chain data.
Tacitscan says bridge confirmation, reflection and destination execution are separate stages.
Tacit says its pool mints public TAC from Bitcoin-origin value and burns it when wrapping back into private notes.
Tacit says each chain action has a small TAC fee shown before the user proceeds.
Tacit lists a 0.002 TAC pool-retained send fee plus a variable leader fee that covers Ethereum gas.
Tacit says users can borrow cUSD against Bitcoin.
Tacit says its chain pool retains part of each fee, increasing the TAC value of its shares.
Tacit’s z0r0z/tacit repository says TAC-vault borrowing has no interest and a one-time fee paid to the operations multisig reserve.
Tacit links to the src-company/tacit GitHub repository as its source channel.
Tacit links to the @tacitfi X account.
Tacit links to a Discord community invite.
Bankless describes an account named ross.wei in connection with a new Tacit project.
GitHub identifies src-company/tacit as a public repository owned by the src-company account.
Ethereum returned the TAC contract name as Tacit Token.

Tacit’s homepage now leads with its live TAC payment chain, settled on Ethereum and connected to Bitcoin.

Tacit’s paper describes a Bitcoin asset-issuance protocol alongside its Ethereum DeFi pool.
Tacit offers TAC-backed dollar and ether borrowing through TACD and TACE vaults deployed on Ethereum mainnet.

Tacit documents a Sepolia Pay-pool mirror for tests, without mainnet funds.

Tacit says farms pay wTAC, redeemable one for one for TAC.
Tacit says cBTC is minted against Bitcoin self-custody locks supported by additional wstETH escrow.
Tacit says borrowing cUSD creates dollar debt secured by cBTC collateral.
Tacit says TAC-vault routers move TAC collateral into vaults and mint TACD or TACE for the borrower.
Tacit says its borrowing engine’s operations multisig can change oracles and borrowing parameters within contract limits.
Tacit says its immutable pool’s lineage steward can create a successor and close the old pool to new value.

differs.why: The 2026 whitepaper says four owners; current on-chain reads and the current specification say five. The paper has no precise revision date, so whether its count is stale or was inaccurate is unanswered. Use the five-owner chain reading for the current configuration.

open_questions: What legal entity, if any, operates Tacit?
Who holds operational authority over components outside the stated immutable pool surface?
Do the MegaETH and Fraxtal Pay-pool deployments have current public usage beyond the documented core contracts?
What checks does the configured operations-wallet executor enforce before it uses its immediate execution privilege?

notes.scope: Whole-project rebuild from F1: payment chain, Bitcoin protocol, DeFi and Pay pools, apps, borrowing components and public project organisation. The current homepage leads with the payment chain; proof availability does not decide prominence.
notes.carry_forward: All 39 F1 line IDs are carried once with their original origins; none dropped. No changes results or panel answers were supplied. F1 was treated as a lead, and its cited primary sources were read afresh. Quotes were shortened; L13’s burn-on-return shorthand is clarified as burning on wrapping back into private notes, from the project’s newer TAC documentation. The upstream repository’s tie is now supported by Bitcoin issuance metadata, so its carried first-party lines are statements rather than external claims.
notes.evidence: Statements are restricted to the project domain or strong/linked channels. External articles, trackers, GitHub platform metadata and Tacitscan remain claims. On-chain reads prove only the values and relationships stated, not blanket privacy, decentralisation or safety. No independent audit was performed.
notes.tokens: TAC is Bitcoin-native and has a canonical metaprotocol asset identifier, not a Bitcoin smart-contract address. To honor the Tokens rule requiring the home-chain contract address, Tokens and its dependent Supply row are omitted rather than placing an Ethereum bridge address on the home chain or calling an asset ID a contract. Native asset and TAC ERC-20 rows give the 21 million genesis issuance and the Ethereum public subset. The Ethereum contract remains in subject.contracts. The bridge identity is checked with the Bitcoin genesis identifier, MINTER, ASSET_ID and the pool asset tuple; it is not LayerZero. The 4.72 million public Ethereum units are a subset, not additional issuance; no confidential balance distribution is inferred. TACD/TACE and cBTC/cUSD are described in lines. wTAC and payment shares are wrappers/receipts, not extra central tokens.
notes.supply_limit: The Bitcoin proof verifies a disclosed genesis commitment opening and zero mint authority against retrieved transaction witness data; it does not replay every later metaprotocol transaction or independently verify Bitcoin consensus. It establishes the original issuance, not current chain-by-chain confidential balances.
notes.status: Live denotes present real-value deployment offered/documented by the project, not a guarantee of availability or safety. MegaETH/Fraxtal have documented core Pay-pool deployments; the public build guide lists only Ethereum/Base/Robinhood. This is a scope difference, not evidence of retirement. Their runtime code was not read in this run. Sepolia is test. Secret Sats signet is past because its current page says testing is switched off; its mainnet product is still offered.
notes.controls: Pool immutability remains a project statement with its stated limits. The lineage steward can retire a generation by creating a successor; current successor is zero. Borrowing is a separate governed surface: engine/vault owner reads match the 2-of-5 wallet. Its normal delay reads one hour, and a contract executor is configured. A simulated call from that executor bypassed signatures, as the multisig code permits; this does not show that an arbitrary user can impersonate it on-chain. The project describes an all-five-signature immediate route, but this run did not verify the executor contract’s internal authorization logic. The paper’s two-of-four description is retained separately from the current five-owner reads as a question-level discrepancy, because its revision date is unclear. No real-world identities are assigned to its owner addresses. The full scope of operational authority is still unanswered; ETHBeat attributes anon.wei app-name/endpoints control to the Z DAO, which is not asserted to operate every Tacit app.
notes.people: No anonymous account is connected to a real name. z0r0z is credited only as the paper’s pseudonymous author; ross.wei is a self-associated account and a Bankless-reported connection, not a proved legal founder. A legal operator is not identified in the reviewed sources. GitHub ownership and app stewardship do not by themselves answer who runs the organisation.
notes.channels: The four supplied channels were rechecked. The home page still links X, src-company/tacit and the Discord invite. Its strong tie is independently supported by TAC contractURI metadata. TAC’s Bitcoin issuance metadata points to github.com/z0r0z/tacit, supporting that additional strong channel. The project’s X bio links tacit.wei.limo. The ross.wei account is self-associated only and has tie none. Discord resolves but did not expose a reliably readable server name beyond the project’s own label.
notes.history: Repeated readings are merged with F1 history; off-chain tracker history uses block null and includes its date in value. The explorer-access question is closed: Etherscan now opens and the deployment transaction/receipt were retrieved. The source’s Ethereum launch date is 18 September; the pool deployment was 17 September. Deployment before announced launch is not a contradiction. Documentation’s suite start block 25998736 is not used as this pool’s creation block; its receipt is 25998751.
notes.outside_sources: Read Bankless’s June article, DefiLlama’s API, Tacitscan, ETHBeat and TokenPost. No evidence warrants treating Tacit as a widely covered project requiring eight outside publishers. ETHBeat discusses Tacit Pay/anon.wei, not the whole DeFi system. TokenPost’s dated prototype introduction is retained with a context link to the current first-party mainnet statement: a launch event is not out-dated by continued operation, and prototype does not itself mean testnet.
